transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what’s been going on that brought you in today?

I guess… work has been the main thing. I’m a camera operator and editor, and lately I keep making these basic technical mistakes I really should not be making—labeling cards wrong, missing timecode notes, things like that.

The one that scared me was exporting a client cut with the wrong lower-third even after I thought I’d checked it. It’s embarrassing. I know better.
How long have you been making these technical mistakes at work?
At this level… probably a little over two years. Around two years and a couple months, I think. It started getting disruptive after the company readjusted how our shoots and edit reviews were run.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?
Not really. I mean, I get frustrated and embarrassed about the work stuff, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling hopeless or like I’ve stopped enjoying things.
Have you been feeling unusually anxious, worried, or on edge about things at work or in your daily life?
Not unusually, no. I mean, I get tense when I know I’ve messed something up, but I don’t think I’m just worried all the time or anything.
Have you noticed any trouble concentrating or making decisions, even about small things, that’s been ongoing lately?

Yeah… mostly with concentrating on the details. I’ll think I’ve checked something, and then I’ve still missed a timecode note or labeled a camera card wrong. The thing that kind of pushed me to come in was exporting a client cut with the wrong lower-third, even though I should’ve caught it.
Have you noticed any decline in your ability to perform your job duties beyond the mistakes you've already mentioned, or have these issues started affecting other areas of your work?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not just the individual mistakes. My producers don’t seem to trust me as much on more complicated shoots now.

And… I was hoping to move toward a senior director of photography role, but that feels like it’s slipping away, even though the actual camera work is still good.

Have you noticed any problems with your memory, attention, or thinking outside of your work tasks, like forgetting appointments, losing track of conversations, or having trouble focusing on reading or TV?

Yeah… I guess attention, more than memory. Like if a producer gives me a note on set, I’ll be looking right at them, but I’m already thinking about the lens change or the next shot. Then I have to ask them to repeat it, which is… not great.
Do you find yourself having trouble focusing or getting distracted easily even when you're not at work, like when you're watching TV or having a conversation with someone?

Yeah… I mean, it happens in conversations. Like on set, a producer will be giving me a note and I’m looking right at them, but I’ve already jumped ahead in my head to the lens change or the next shot. Then I have to ask them to repeat it, which feels pretty embarrassing.
Do you also find it hard to focus on things outside of work, like when you're trying to watch a show, read something, or do a task around the house?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid as much attention to that outside of work. I guess nothing stands out to me the same way.
When you're at home or in other non-work settings, do you ever find yourself losing track of what's being said in a conversation or missing details because your mind is elsewhere?

Mostly I notice it at work. Like I said, someone will be talking right to me—giving me a note—and I’m… already somewhere else in my head, thinking about the next setup. Then I have to ask them to repeat it, which feels awkward. At home, I don’t know, I haven’t really tracked it as much.
Do you often feel restless, as if you can't sit still, or find yourself needing to be constantly doing something?

Yeah… I do. It’s mostly in situations where I’m supposed to just sit and watch, like a client screening. I can do it, but it feels like this pressure building under my skin, like I need to get up or do something with my body. I try to keep it contained, but it’s there.
Outside of work, do you find yourself losing focus or feeling restless in situations where you’re supposed to sit still or pay attention, like during meetings, conversations, or watching something?

Yeah… more the restless part than losing focus, I think. Like if I’m supposed to sit quietly and just watch something, I can feel this kind of pressure building, like I need to get up or move or do something with my body. I try not to make it obvious.
